findings.title: PyMC is a direct runtime dependency but is not declared in pyproject.toml
findings.command: python3 -c "import tomllib; d=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb')); print(d['project']['dependencies'])" && grep -rln '^import pymc' src/ | wc -l
findings.expected: PyMC (the library that performs every fit: pm.fit, pm.sample, pm.find_MAP, prior/posterior predictive) is declared in [project.dependencies] with a version bound, as are the other directly imported runtime packages (numpy, pandas, arviz).
findings.observed: Declared dependencies = ['scikit-learn~=1.8.0', 'pymc-extras==0.7.0', 'blackjax==1.3']; no 'pymc' entry. 8 source files import pymc directly (grep -rln '^import pymc' src/ | wc -l -> 8), including src/vangja/time_series.py:24. PyMC can only arrive transitively via pymc-extras/blackjax, whose resolved version is not declared.
findings.consequence: The environment that produces every sampled result is not reconstructible from the package metadata: `pip install vangja` may resolve a different PyMC than the one used for reported numbers, and the README/container separately mandate an unpinned `pymc>=5.27.1`. Results cannot be attributed to a declared PyMC version.

findings.title: No lockfile; container and CI install floating PyMC while docs claim 'bit-for-bit reproducibility'
findings.command: find . -not -path './.git/*' \( -iname '*lock*' -o -iname 'requirements*.txt' -o -iname 'environment*.yml' \) | grep -v __pycache__; grep -n 'pymc>=\|pip install' case_studies/singularity.def; grep -n 'bit-for-bit' case_studies/README.md
findings.expected: An exact-pinned lock/manifest (with hashes) for the environment that produced the reported experiments; the image installs that locked set or records `conda list --explicit`/`pip freeze`; any 'bit-for-bit' claim is backed by it.
findings.observed: No lockfile, requirements file or environment file exists at the snapshot (find output empty). singularity.def:37 installs `python=3.13 "pymc>=5.27.1"` and then an unpinned `pip install --no-cache-dir --retries 5 --timeout 120 '/vangja[reproducibility]'` (lower bound only). case_studies/README.md:3 asserts the setup ensures **bit-for-bit reproducibility** of all experiments reported in the accompanying paper. .github/workflows/docs.yml likewise runs `pip install pymc>=5.27.1`.
findings.consequence: Two image builds on different dates can resolve different PyMC/NumPy/Numba/statsmodels versions, changing sampler and optimizer numerics. The documented 'bit-for-bit reproducibility' claim is unsupported, and reported metrics cannot be exactly regenerated.
evidence: case_studies/README.md:3 '... ensures **bit-for-bit reproducibility** of all experiments reported in the accompanying paper.'

findings.title: fit() exposes no random_seed and passes none to pm.sample/pm.fit/find_MAP; no seed recorded in runners, SLURM or container
findings.command: grep -rn 'random_seed' src/ case_studies/ .github/ || echo NO_RANDOM_SEED; sed -n '440,451p' src/vangja/time_series.py
findings.expected: fit() takes a random_seed argument (and/or the runners set and log one); every sampler call (pm.sample, pm.fit, find_MAP, sample_prior_predictive, sample_posterior_predictive) receives and records it so NUTS/VI draws are repeatable and auditable.
findings.observed: 'NO_RANDOM_SEED' (grep finds zero occurrences in src/, case_studies/, .github/). fit() signature (line 280-297) has no seed parameter. pm.sample is called with samples/chains/cores/nuts_sampler/initvals/step/progressbar only (lines 440-450) and pm.fit with n/method/start/progressbar only (line 425); neither receives random_seed. The smart-home runner trains its NUTS base models with `temp_model.fit(train_temp_df, scaler=scaler, method="nuts", samples=1000)` (run.py:76) with no seed, and submit_ablation.slurm defines no SEED variable.
findings.consequence: Every NUTS-based number in the reported case studies (including metrics.csv, whose transfer-learning target models condition on the NUTS base-model posterior) is non-deterministic and cannot be reproduced or attributed to a seed. No run record allows replay.

findings.title: Case-study results are appended without any run provenance and silently merged across environments
findings.command: grep -n 'version\|rev-parse\|sha\|seed\|timestamp\|git' case_studies/smart_home/run.py || echo NONE; head -1 case_studies/smart_home/metrics.csv
findings.expected: Each result row (or a sidecar manifest) records the code revision (git SHA), vangja/PyMC versions, seed and command, so every metric is attributable to the environment that produced it.
findings.observed: grep -> NONE: run.py writes no version, commit, seed or timestamp. metrics.csv header = timeseries,start_date,use_temp_df,hierarchical,uniform_constant,tune_method,tune_loss_factor,shrinkage_strength,intercept_sd,beta_sd,scaler,mse,rmse,mae,mape. On restart, rows are skipped purely on a hyperparameter tuple match (processed_experiments set, lines 105-135) and new rows are appended.
findings.consequence: metrics.csv is not provenance-tracked; a resumed run after code/env changes silently mixes results from different software in one file, and no row can be tied to the code that produced the headline numbers.
evidence: metrics.csv header contains only experiment parameters and metrics
run.py:105-135 resume skip set keyed on hyperparameters only

findings.title: Both case-study datasets are downloaded from mutable Kaggle datasets with no revision or hash pinning
findings.command: grep -n 'dataset_download' -A2 src/vangja/datasets/loaders.py; grep -rn 'sha256\|md5\|hash' src/vangja/datasets/loaders.py || echo NO_HASH_CHECK
findings.expected: The exact dataset revision is pinned (kagglehub revision) and/or a content hash is verified and recorded for the reported runs, so changed upstream data cannot silently change results.
findings.observed: kagglehub.dataset_download('selfishgene/historical-hourly-weather-data') and kagglehub.dataset_download('taranvee/smart-home-dataset-with-weather-information') are called with the dataset handle only -- no revision, no hash. grep for sha256/md5/hash in loaders.py -> NO_HASH_CHECK.
findings.consequence: Both case-study inputs (temperature base series and smart-home target series) are fetched unpinned from mutable upstream datasets; a re-download can change train/test values and all reported metrics with no detection or audit trail.

findings.title: SLURM job records no code revision, container hash, package freeze or seed
findings.command: grep -n -i 'seed\|rev-parse\|sha\|freeze\|pip list\|conda list\|version' case_studies/submit_ablation.slurm || echo NONE
findings.expected: The job log records the vangja git SHA (and image SHA-256) plus the package environment (pip/conda freeze) and sampler seed, so a completed run's outputs can be tied to inputs.
findings.observed: grep -> NONE. The script echoes only job id, hostname, CPUs, case study, mode, script and start date, then runs `singularity exec --bind ... case_studies/vangja.sif python ${SCRIPT_PATH}`; the image is referenced by mutable path only and no revision/version/seed is captured.
findings.consequence: Completed HPC jobs cannot be attributed to a code revision or image content; reruns after any repo or image change are indistinguishable, defeating audit of the reported ablation runs.
evidence: submit_ablation.slurm:80-100 job info block lists only job/node/CPU/mode/script/date
singularity exec uses path case_studies/vangja.sif with no digest

findings.title: Documented one-command reproduction invokes scripts that do not exist at the snapshot
findings.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; print({m: (Path('case_studies/smart_home')/m).exists() for m in ['ablation_fast.py','ablation_full.py','classical_baselines.py','run.py','run_classical_baselines.py']})"
findings.expected: `sbatch case_studies/submit_ablation.slurm smart_home fast|full|classical` and `python case_studies/smart_home/classical_baselines.py` run the scripts the docs and SLURM mode map name.
findings.observed: Output: {'ablation_fast.py': False, 'ablation_full.py': False, 'classical_baselines.py': False, 'run.py': True, 'run_classical_baselines.py': True}. submit_ablation.slurm maps fast->ablation_fast.py, full->ablation_full.py, classical->classical_baselines.py and exits with 'ERROR: Script not found' for all three modes; smart_home/README.md:18 and case_studies/README.md:130-138 document exactly those commands.
findings.consequence: The documented reproduction path fails at its first step for every mode; there is no documentation-consistent way to regenerate the classical-baseline results (results_classical/*) from this snapshot.
evidence: command output: {'ablation_fast.py': False, 'ablation_full.py': False, 'classical_baselines.py': False, 'run.py': True, 'run_classical_baselines.py': True}
